sections.overview: Mediothele australis is a mygalomorph spider in the family Hexathelidae, native to Chile; the World Spider Catalog accepts the genus in that family.
sections.identification: It was originally described from an adult male, and its female was formally described later using diagnostic anatomical characters.
sections.habitat: It is known from Chile, including central and southern records, but its precise habitat and range are poorly documented.
sections.diet: No species-specific prey records were found; it is a predatory spider, but a more detailed diet cannot be established from the reviewed sources.
sections.behavior: The sources consulted focus on taxonomy and morphology, so behavior and web structure remain undocumented here.
sections.reproduction: The reviewed catalog and description papers provide no species-specific reproductive observations.
sections.ecology: The original description established Mediothele from Chile, and later taxonomic work added several congeners while retaining M. australis as the type species.
sections.conservation: No global conservation assessment or population trend was located in the sources consulted.
